spans.s:
नश् 1. नश् (related to rt. नक्ष्; cf. rt.
1. अश्), cl. 1. P. A. नशति, -ते, Aor.
आनट् or आनक्, &c. (Pāṇ.

, but these forms
may be referred to rt. 1. अश्), Ved. to reach, attain,
[]
obtain; to meet with, find; Caus. नशयति, &c., to
cause to obtain or meet with; [cf. Lat. nanciscor.]

नश् 2. नश्, cl. 1. 4. (more usually cl.
4.) P. नशति, नश्यति (ep. also -ते),
ननाश (3rd pl. नेशुस्), नशिता, नंष्टा (accord-
ing to Vopa-deva also नङ्ग्धा), नशिष्यति, नङ्क्-
ष्यति, अनशत्, अनेशत्, नशितुम्, नंष्टुम्, to be
lost, disappear, to become invisible, to vanish; to
perish, be destroyed, wane; to escape, run away;
to come to nothing, be frustrated, be unsuccessful:
Caus. नाशयति (ep. also A. नाशयते), -यितुम्,
Aor. अनीनशत्, to cause to disappear, make invisible;
to cause to perish, suffer to perish, destroy, efface;
to violate, deflower; to cause to be lost, to lose; to
forget; to extinguish (as a fire); to drive away, cause
to fly away; to disappear (in मा व्याघ्रा नीनशुर्
वनात्, let not the tigers disappear from the forest,
Mahā-bh. Udyoga-p. 862): Desid. निनशिषति, नि-
नङ्क्षति: Intens. नानश्यते, नानंष्टि; [cf.
Zend naśu, ‘a corpse;’ naś-ista, ‘very destructive:’
Gr. νέκ-υ-ς, νέκυ-ια, νεκ-ρό-ς, probably νόσο-ς,
νοῦσο-ς for νοξο-ς, like συν for ξυν: Lat. nex, nec-
are, noc-ēre, noxa, per-nicies, ve-ne-nu-m for ve-
nec-nu-m: Goth. nau-s, navi-s, ‘a corpse,’ for nag-
u-s or nah-u-s.]

3. नश्, क्, क्, क्, or ट्, ट्, ट्, disappearing; perishing;
[cf. जीव-न्˚.]

नस् 1. नस् (the alternative form for अस्मान्
acc. pl., for अस्मभ्यम् dat. pl., and for अस्माकम्
gen. pl. of the first personal pronoun अस्मद्, q. v.),
us, to us, of us; (नस् is an enclitic and has no
accent.)

नस् 2. नस्, cl. 1. A. नसते, नेसे, नसिता,
&c., Ved. to approach, to go towards, to
join; to copulate (especially as husband and wife);
(said to mean also) to be crooked or curved; to bend;
to be fraudulent; [cf. Gr. νέ-ο-μαι, νίσ-σ-ο-μαι,
νόσ-το-ς, probably also ναίω for νασ-_y_-ω, ἔ-νασ-σα,
ἐ-νάσ-θη-ν.]

नस् 3. नस्, f. (probably fr. rt. स्ना, to
bathe, or स्नु, to flow, the initial स् being dropped;
cf. नौ; नस् is defective in nom. voc. sing. du. and
pl., acc. sing. du., but may be optionally substituted for
नासिका, q. v., in the acc. pl. and remaining cases, e. g.
नसस् or नासिकास्, नसा or नासिकया, नोभ्याम् or
नासिकाभ्याम्; only the weak cases नसा, नसि, न-
सोस्, however, appear to occur), the nose; [cf. नासा,
नासिका; Lat. nasus, naris.]
—नः-क्षुद्र, अस्, आ,
अम्, small-nosed.
—नस्तः-कर्मन्, अ, n. ‘the put-
ting into the nose,’ taking snuff.
—नस्-तस्, ind. from
the nose, into the nose.
—नस्य्-ओत, अस्, आ, अम्, (fr.
नसि loc. sing. + ओत), led by a string through the
septum of the nose, fastened by the nose, furnished
with a nose-ring; an ox or other animal led by a
string through the septum of the nose.
—नस्-वत्,
आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. having a nose.

नास् 1. नास्, cl. 1. A. नासते, ननासे,
नासितुम्, to sound.

नास् 2. नास्, Ved. the nose, in नासा, du.
(Ṛg-veda

1. नश in दू-णश, दुर्-णश, q. v.; [cf. 1.
नाश.]

2. नश, अस्, m. destruction; perishing; [cf. 2.
नाश.]

नस (at the end of an adj. comp.) = 3. नस्, the
nose, see उन्-न्˚, उरू-ण्˚, कुम्भी-न्˚, खर-ण्˚,
गो-न्˚, द्रु-ण्˚, &c.; (आ), f. the nose.

नाश 1. नाश, अस्, m. (fr. rt. 1. नश्), Ved.
attainment, obtaining; [cf. दू-णाश.]

नाश 2. नाश, अस्, m. (fr. rt. 2. नश्), dis-
appearance; destruction, annihilation, ruin, loss;
death; misfortune; abandonment, desertion; flight,
retreat; (in arithmetic) elimination; [cf. कर्म-न्˚,
ग्रह-न्˚, चित्त-न्˚, दू-णाश.]
—नाश-तस्, ind. =
नाशात्, from death.

नासा, f. (said by some to be fr. rt. स्ना = rt. स्नु),
the nose, (originally perhaps नासा, sing. = a nostril;
नासे, du. = the two nostrils or the nose); a pro-
boscis, the trunk of an elephant [cf. गज-न्˚]; a
piece of wood over a door projecting like a nose,
the upper timber of a door [cf. नक्र]; the plant
Gendarussa Vulgaris (= वासक); [cf. Lat. nāsus,
nāris for nāsis; Old Germ. nāsa; Angl. Sax. nāse;
Mod. Germ. nāse; Slav. nōsŭ; Lith. nōsis; Gr. νῆ-
σος; Hib. neas, ‘a promontory,’ ness in Dunge-ness.]
—नासाग्र (˚सा-अग्˚), अस्, m. the point or tip of
the nose.
—नासा-छिद्र, अम्, n. a nostril.
—नासा-
छिन्नी, f. a species of bird with a divided beak (=
पूर्णिका).
—नासा-ज्वर, अस्, m. a kind of disease
of the nose (= नक्र).
—नासा-दक्षिणावर्त
(˚ण-आव्˚), अस्, m. wearing the nose-ring in the right
nostril by rich women who have children (?).
—नासा-
दारु, n. = नासा, a piece of wood over a door pro-
jecting like a nose; the upper timber of a door-frame.
—नासा-नाह, अस्, m. thickening of the membrane
of the nose, stoppage of the nostrils.
—नासान्तिक,
अस्, आ, अम् (fr. नासा-अन्त), reaching to the nose; [cf.
केशान्तिक.]
—नासा-परिशोष, अस्, m. heat and
dryness of the nose.
—नासा-परिस्राव, अस्, m. ‘nose-
flow,’ running at the nose, a running cold.
—नासा-
पाक, अस्, m. a kind of disease of the nose attended
with inflammation.
—नासा-पुट, अस्, m. ‘nose-cup,’
the outside of the nostril, the nostril.
—नासापुट-
मर्यादा, f. the septum of the nose.
—नासा-प्र-
तीनाह, अस्, m. = नासा-नाह, thickening of the
membrane of the nose, stoppage of the nostrils.
—नासा-रक्त-पित्त, अम्, n. bleeding of the nose.
—नासा-रन्ध्र, अम्, n. ‘nose-aperture,’ the
nostril.
—नासार्शस् (˚सा-अर्˚), आस्, m. polypus of the
nose.
—नासा-वंश, अस्, m. the bridge of the nose.
—नासा-वामावर्त (˚म-आव्˚), अस्, m. wearing the
nose-ring in the left nostril, a mark of sorrow or
distress.
—नासा-विवर, अस्, m. ‘nose-cavity,’ a
nostril.
—नासा-शोष, अस्, m. dryness of the nostrils.
—नासा-संवेदन, अस्, m. Momordica Charantia
(= काण्डीर-लता).
—नासा-स्राव, अस्, m. = नासा-
परिस्राव, ‘nose-flow,’ running at the nose, a
running cold.

नशन, अम्, n. disappearing, vanishing; perishing;
escaping.

नाशन, अस्, ई, अम्, destroying, annihilating,
causing to be lost, causing to perish, removing,
(commonly in comp. with the object; cf. दुःस्वप्-
न-न्˚); (अम्), n. destruction, removing, removal,
expulsion; ruin, perishing; forgetting.

नशितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, one who disappears; perishing,
being lost; destroying, a destroyer; [cf. नंष्टृ.]

नश्यत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, perishing, decaying, being
destroyed; waning, wasting.
—नश्यत्-प्रसूति, इस्,
इस्, इ, whose offspring perishes; (इस्), f. a woman
who brings forth a dead child.
—नश्यत्प्रसूतिका,
f. a female bearing a dead child.

नश्वर, अस्, ई, अम्, perishing, perishable; de-
structible; transitory, evanescent, subject to decay;
destructive, mischievous.
—नश्वर-त्व, अम्, n.
perishableness, transitoriness; destructiveness.

नष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, lost, disappeared, disappearing;
vanished, invisible, lost sight of; perished, destroyed,
ruined, spoiled, wasted, annihilated, dead; run away,
fled; depraved, debauched; deprived of (at the
beginning of a comp.).
—नष्ट-चन्द्र, अस्,
m., N. of the fourth day in both halves of the
month Bhādra.
—नष्ट-चेतन, अस्, आ, अम्, one
who has lost consciousness, unconscious, fainted, in-
sensible, swooning away, losing one's senses.
—नष्-
ट-चेष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, one who has lost the power
of motion; unconscious, fainted, insensible.
—नष्-
टचेष्ट-ता, f. unconsciousness, insensibility, faint-
ing, swooning.
—नष्ट-जन्मन्, अ, n. ‘the lost
nativity,’ subsequent calculation or casting of a lost
nativity.
—नष्ट-जातक, अम्, n. = नष्ट-जन्-
मन्; N. of the thirteenth Adhyāya in Varāha-
mihira's Laghu-jātaka.
—नष्ट-दृष्टि, इस्, इस्, इ,
one who has lost his sight, blind.
—नष्ट-मति,
इस्, इस्, इ, one who has lost his intellects.
—नष्ट-
मार्गण, अम्, n. seeking any lost object.
—नष्ट-
राज्य, अम्, n., N. of a district to the north-east of
Madhya-deśa.
—नष्ट-रूप, अस्, आ, अम्, one whose
form is lost or no more seen; (आ), f., scil. अनु-
ष्टुभ्, a variety of the Anu-ṣṭubh.
—नष्ट-
विष, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. (a snake &c.) that has lost
(its) venom.
—नष्ट-वीज, अस्, आ, अम्, destitute
of the seminal secretion, without the power of pro-
creating, impotent.
—नष्ट-वेदन, अस्, ई, अम्,
finding a lost object.
—नष्ट-संस्मृति, इस्, इस्, इ,
one who has lost his memory, unmindful, forgetful.
—नष्ट-सञ्ज्ञ, अस्, आ, अम्, one who has lost
his consciousness.
—नष्ट-स्मृति, इस्, इस्, इ, one
who has lost his memory, forgetful.
—नष्टाग्नि
(˚ट-अग्˚), इस्, m. a Brāhman or householder whose
fire has been extinguished or who has lost his conse-
crated fire.
—नष्टातङ्कम् (˚ट-आत्˚), ind. without
[]
anxiety or fear.
—नष्टात्मन् (˚ट-आत्˚), आ, आ, अ,
deprived of mind or sense.
—नष्टाप्ति-सूत्र (˚ट-
आप्˚), अम्, n. booty, plunder.
—नष्टार्थ (˚ट-अर्˚),
अस्, आ, अम्, one who has lost his property, reduced
to poverty.
—नष्टाशङ्क (˚ट-आश्˚), अस्, आ, अम्,
destitute of fear, fearless, dauntless.
—नष्टासु
(˚ट-असु), उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. one whose vital spirits
have disappeared.
—नष्टेन्दु-कला (˚ट-इन्˚), f. the
day of new moon when it rises invisible.
—नष्टेन्-
द्रिय (˚ट-इन्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, one who has lost his
organs of sense, deprived of one's senses.
—नष्-
टैषिन् (˚ट-एष्˚), ई, इणी, इ, seeking any lost object.
—नष्टैष्य, अम्, n. the act of seeking what
has been lost.
नष्ट नष्ट. See p. 473, col. 3.
नष्टि, इस्, f. loss, destruction, ruin.
नशाक नशाक, अस्, m. a species of crow.

नाशक, अस्, आ, अम्, destroying, destructive, anni-
hilating, causing to perish; [cf. कु-न्˚, कृत-न्˚.]
नसि, the nose (?), in कुम्भी-न्˚, q. v.
नाशी, f., N. of a river near Benares.

नस्त, अस्, m. the nose; (आ), f. a hole bored
in the septum of the nose, cf. नस्तक, नस्-
तित; (अम्), n. a sternutatory, snuff.
—नस्त-
करण, अम्, n. a kind of instrument used by the
Bhikṣus for injecting the nose.
—नस्त-तस्, ind.
(perhaps only = नस्-तस् with reduplicated affix तस्),
from the nose, out of the nose.
—नस्तोत (˚त-
ओत), अस्, m. an ox led by a string through his nose;
(also read नस्य्-ओत; see under 3. नस्.)

नस्तक, अस्, m. a hole bored in the septum or
bridge of the nose of cattle for draught.

नस्तित, अस्, आ, अम्, nozzled, having a hole bored
in the septum of the nose, an ox or any other
draught animal with a string through its nose, (the
sort of rein usually employed in India.)

नस्य, अस्, आ, अम्, belonging or relating to the
nose, nasal, in the nose; (आ), f. the nose; the string
through the nose of an animal [cf. नास्य]; (अम्),
n. the hairs in the nose; a sternutatory, snuff.
—नस्य-विधि, इस्, m. ‘rules about sternutatories,’
N. of the twenty-seventh chapter of the medical
work Śārṅgadhara-saṃhitā.

नाश्य, अस्, आ, अम्, liable to be destroyed, de-
structible.

नास्य, अम्, n. a nose-cord, the rein of a draught-ox
passed through the septum of the nostrils; (perhaps
collectively) noses, a multitude of noses (?); [cf.
नस्य.]

नसंविद् न-संविद्, त्, f. unconsciousness;
forgetfulness.

नसुकर न-सुकर, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, not easy
to be done.

नाशनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, liable to be destroyed,
destructible.

नाशयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, destroying, annihilating,
removing.

नाशयितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, Ved. a destroyer, remov-
ing, a remover.

नाशित, अस्, आ, अम्, destroyed, ruined, suffered to
perish, lost.

नाशिन्, ई, इनी, इ, destructive, destroying, a de-
stroyer; removing; perishing, perishable, being lost
or destroyed; [cf. अनर्थ-न्˚, कुष्ठ-न्˚, क्ष-
य-न्˚.]

नाशुक, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. disappearing, perishing,
being lost.

नाष्टिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. नष्ट), belonging or
relating to anything lost; (अस्), m. the owner of
anything lost, the former owner of a lost chattel.

नाष्ट्रा, f., Ved. danger, destruction; an evil
spirit, a demon.

नासालु, उस्, m. a tree, commonly Kāyaphal.
See कट्फल, p. 196, col. 1.

नासिका, f. the nose, (originally नासिका, sing. = a
nostril; नासिके, du. = the two nostrils or the nose);
the trunk of an elephant; a proboscis; any nose-
shaped object [cf. चर्म-न्˚]; a projection, the
upper timber of a door; an epithet of the nymph
Aśvinī; [cf. अ-नासिक, काक-नासिका, चर्म-न्˚.]
—नासिक-त्र्यम्बक-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a sa-
cred bathing-place mentioned in the Rasika-ramaṇa.
—नासिकन्-धम, अस्, आ, अम् (नासिकम् for acc.
sing. नासिकाम्), blowing or breathing through the
nose, snoring, &c.
—नासिकन्-धय, अस्, ई, अम्
(नासिकम् for acc. sing. नासिकाम्), drinking through
the nose.
—नासिक-वत्, आन्, अती, अत् (for नासिका-
वत्), Ved. having a nose.
—नासिकाग्र (˚क-अग्˚),
अम्, n. the tip of the nose.
—नासिका-पाक, अस्, m.
= नासा-पाक, a kind of disease or inflammation of
the nose.
—नासिका-पुट, अस्, m. = नासा-पुट,
‘nose-cup,’ the outside of the nostril, the nostril.
—नासिका-मल, अम्, n. the mucus of the nose,
snot.
नासिका नासिका. See p. 480, col. 3.
नासिक्यक, अम्, n. the nose.

नासत्य नासत्य, अस्, m. (derived by native
commentators fr. न + अ-सत्य, ‘not untrue,’ or fr.
नासा + affix त्य, or still more improbably fr. ना,
nom. of नृ = नेतृ + सत्य), N. of one of the
Aśvins, the other being then called Dasra; (औ), m.
du. the common N. of the two Aśvins, see अश्विनौ;
(आ), f. the constellation Aśvinī; (अस्, आ, अम्), re-
ferring or relating to the Nāsatyas; [cf. Zend nā-
onhaitya.]

नासमौजस नासमौजस (न-अस्˚), अस्, m.,
N. of the brother of Asamaujas and son of Kambala-
barhiṣa.

नासीर नासीर, अम्, n. advancing or skir-
mishing in front of an army, leaving the line and
defying or challenging the enemy by shouts and
gestures; (अस्), m. the van or a champion who
advances before the line; (also read नासिर.)

नास्ति नास्ति (न-अस्ति), ind. non-existence,
not so, it is not.
—नास्ति-ता, f. or नास्ति-त्व, अम्, n.
non-existence.
—नास्ति-वाद, अस्, m. “assertion of ‘it
is not’ or of non-existence,” infidelity.

नास्तिक, अस्, ई, अम्, atheistical, unbelieving, infidel,
an unbeliever, applied by the orthodox Hindūs to
any one who denies the divine authority of the
Vedas and a future life, or doubts the legends of the
Purāṇas; [cf. आस्तिक.]
—नास्तिक-ता, f. or नास्तिक-
त्व, अम्, n. or नास्तिक्य, अम्, n. infidelity, disbelief,
atheism, denial of the deity, of a future state, of the
authority of the Vedas, &c.; Buddhism, heresy, &c.
—नास्तिक-मत, अम्, n. an atheistical opinion.

नास्तिद नास्तिद or (according to others)
नास्तितद, अस्, m. the mango tree (= आम्र).
